paper.title: The mass and density of the dwarf planet (225088) 2007 OR10
paper.rights: Specific arXiv record uses nonexclusive distribution, not CC BY. ESA/Hubble image CC BY 4.0 does not license this paper or its figures. No figure embedded. Final publisher version/publication chronology not audited.

inspection.visual: Rendered pages 4–7 inspected, including Tables 1–3 and density discussion. Targeted sections 2–6; not a full visual audit of all pages or reproduction of the reduction.

observations.recovery: HST proposal 15207, PI Alex H. Parker, four October/December 2017 epochs, WFC3 UVIS2-C512C-SUB. Alternating F350LP and F606W/F814W, same-filter comoving coadds, TinyTim/DAOPHOT reduction described by authors, not reproduced.
observations.limits: Printed MJD values retained without UTC conversion; time standard/raw products/exposure/coadd/PSF and exact opo1718b collage crosswalk remain open. J2000 relative astrometry is not a surface frame or current ephemeris. Publisher pixel-scale statements are not new raster computations.

orbit.limits: Mirror orbit alternatives remain unresolved. Mass is system mass, not independently measured primary-only mass. Orbit period is not primary or satellite spin; no locking, permanent face, normal or dated observer registration established.

thermal.inputs: Herschel PACS 70/100/160 micron fluxes from Pal et al. 2016; constant emissivity 0.9; thermal-inertia trials 0.1–50 J m^-2 s^-1/2 K^-1; roughness 0.1–0.3 RMS slope. H_V=2.34±0.05 in thermal section.
thermal.geometry: Equator-on, pole-on, orbit-aligned sphere and ellipsoid trials. Coplanar primary equator/satellite orbit is assumed, not a measured spin pole. All cases have acceptable reduced chi-square <=1.
thermal.alternatives: Table 3 pole-on sphere 1158±32 km, albedo .16±.01, density 2.15±.17 g/cm3; equator-on sphere 1531 km, .09, density .92(+.46,-.14). Ellipsoid cases are model alternatives, not measured axes. Authors prefer approximately spherical 22.4h, variegated albedo and aligned equator, but radiometric data alone do not uniquely select the models.
thermal.limits: Model diameters/albedos and derived density do not establish local chemistry, porosity fractions, visible colour or geography. Pluto/Charon thermal comparisons are not skins. No regional pattern or spectrum transferred.

reportedInconsistencies.density: Abstract reports diameter 1230±50 km and density 1.75±0.07 g/cm3; section 6 reports aligned-sphere density 1.74±0.16 and Table 3 1.73–1.80±0.16. Preserve each reported value; uncertainty difference not resolved.
reportedInconsistencies.ranking: Abstract calls object fifth most massive after Eris, Pluto, Haumea and Makemake; section 3 calls it fourth after Eris, Pluto and Haumea. Cause unresolved; neither adopted as an exhaustive current ranking.
